steps.text: Combine lime juice, olive oil, garlic, salt, and oregano in a large resealable plastic bag. Seal the bag and shake until well combined. Taste marinade for tartness: if too tart, add a little more oil; if not enough zing, add more lime juice. The garlic and salt flavors should also be noticeable, but not overpowering. Place tenderloins into the bag, seal, and turn to coat. Marinate in the refrigerator for 2 to 5 hours.
Remove tenderloins from marinade and shake off excess. Discard remaining marinade.
Preheat an outdoor grill for medium heat and lightly oil the grate.

Grill tenderloins on the preheated grill for 20 to 30 minutes, turning once, or to desired doneness. An instant-read thermometer inserted into the center should read at least 145 degrees F (63 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Greek Pork Tenderloin
raw_recipe.description: This Greek-style pork tenderloin features a zesty marinade of olive oil, garlic, fresh lime juice, and oregano which makes it super tender!

review.reviewBody: I also halved the recipe, et it marinate overnight, cooked it in a 350 degree oven for about 45 mins. It was perfect -- so moist and tender. Plus, the leftovers make great Greek pita sandwiches with lettuce, tomatoes, olives, feta, red onion, pepperocini and greek dressing. Yum!

This was delicious! Halved it like some suggested. I wasn't prepared to grill so I seared it for 10 minutes and then cooked it in the oven at 400 for 30min. I also left some marinade and added some tomatoes to the dish half way through. When finished. I sliced it and laid it on a bed of salad with the marinade as a dressing with some tomatoes. Was so tender and flavorful. Will repeat!

Some of the best meat I've ever cooked!! I did mine a little differently than instructed. First I had adjusted the servings to 4. I ran out of lime juice, so I only put in 1/2 a cup and it was the perfect tartness. I think following the recipe would have been too much. I used Italian seasoning instead of oregano because it's what I had. I put the tenderloin in my crock pot and dumped the marinade over it. I rubbed it all over the loin and let it sit in the crock pot in the fridge all night. Then, in the morning I started the crock pot on low and let it cook all day (8 hours). It was tender and delicious. I've already sent the recipe to several people to make.

This one is a solid 4 1/2 for me. I really loved the tang from the lime juice, it was such a different flavor than I'm used to for pork. I had this as both dinner and used some for an egg scramble the next day.

I did make a couple of minor changes. I was unable to get pork tenderloins, so I used a 3 1/2 lb pork roast that I split before marinating, and due to apartment living, I was unable to grill, so I baked at 350 for 45-60 minutes. I did also let marinate for 2 days, not just overnight as I normally do.

We loved this! I have never had a pork loin come out so tender and juicy. I used just one pork loin, so cut the marinade down. As suggested, I made just one sixth of the marinade called for and it was plenty. Only changes I made were increasing the garlic a tad and adding a sprinkle of thyme. I roasted in the oven because it was too cold to grill out. 425 for 30 minutes, finished off with broiler on Low.

This is a great combination! It does make a lot of marinade, so as one other person mentioned, only use use 1/3 of the marinade ingredients. I only made one 1-lb tenderloin so I actually used 1/6 of the recipe and it was PLENTY. I also only marinated for an hour, and baked the tenderloin with the marinade. Came out super moist and flavorful, the lime really comes through but the other ingredients still make it taste like a true Greek dish.

I have tried many pork loin recipes and this is, hands down, the best! My family loved it!! I followed others advice and used fresh onion and garlic. Baked in the over at 400 for 40 minutes. It was perfectly done.

Excellent marinade for pork tenderloin - however I cut the amount of marinade in half and it was plenty for 2 pound of pork. I used lemon juice instead of lime about 1/2 cup and cut the salt back to 1/2 tsp. I used only 2 Tbsp. of oregano. I added 1/4 cup of low sodium soy sauce. I cut the pork into kabobs, put everything into a ziploc bag and let it marinate all day. It grilled up perfectly and tasted great!

NOTE: This is WAY TOO MUCH marinade for 2 pounds of pork. I used 1/3 of all ingredients (except the pork), and it was plenty for 2 pounds of pork! (If you change the serving size of this recipe to yield 2 instead of 6, you will have the right proportions.)

I also added 2 T. of sugar and a dash of pepper. It came out great! 

I was looking for a marinade free of soy (soy sauce, teriyaki, etc.), and this is perfect. We make this all the time now! We usually cut up the pork into large cubes before marinating, and then grill them as kabobs with green peppers, cherry tomatoes, and pineapple. Always a favorite in our house--and we never have any leftover!

This came out great using the recommended modifications. I used mostly lemon juice and just a few tablespoons of lime juice. I also used dried oregano straight from my brother-in-law's backyard in Greece (it grows wild and abundantly). I prepped the marinade the night before so the flavors could marry. Then I poured it over the meat inside a ziploc baggie and massage the meat a lil. I worry about over-marinating meat especially when it has a lot of acid like fresh lime/lemon so that is why I didn't do it overnight. This marinated all day until I got home from work (about 10 hours). I grilled it on med-high to sear in the juices (3-4 minutes each side) and then turned it on low for about 15 additional minutes turning once. It was juicy and flavorful. Served with a greek pasta salad and some crusty bread.

This was fabulous! I used only 1/3 of the marinade, let it sit for about 4 hours, and it was perfect for one tenderloin. I started by searing it on all sides on the stovetop, then roasting it in the marinade for about 20-25 minutes (very unscientific) at 400. It was so juicy and delicious! Used some fresh meyer lemons and fresh oregano. I thought the marinade was going to be too strong when I first made it, but it turned out so good. A great alternative to apples, sweet potatoes, and maple syrup. Goes great with a Greek salad.
I halved the marinade but the family didn't like it. I wouldn't make it again.
I did halve it and did one sixth of recipe marinade but it was great-took our barbecue the full 30 minutes. Easy, fast, and yummy.
Been making this for years. Amazing recipe!!
No salt, cut the measurement for lime juice & olive oil in half ... grilled on stovetop...
It was a hit with my family. We call it a keeper.
Made as suggested. Would make again. Loved the lemon.
The only deviation that I made form the recipe is that I gave it a really light brush of honey about 3 minutes before I pulled it off the grill. Highly recommend.
Easy and delicious. Try to marinate it as long as overnight. It does make a tender piece of meat even more tender.

I don't see why many rave about this. I used lemon juice instead of lime juice, but that was the only deviation from the recipe. I marinated it for about 7 hours and then grilled it. It had an overwhelming lemon flavor.
